transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-11-25
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Jared (CTO - Acme), Priya (ML Eng), Liam (DevOps)
Links shared: https://rwd.co/poc-docs-acme (POC doc), https://rwd.co/bench-acme (benchmark sheet)

Summary:
Quick check-in on onboarding progress, access setup (VPC/SSO), environment readiness for benchmark runs, and tuning items (batching/quant). Agreed next steps and owners.

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we'll keep this to ~45 minutes. Quick roll call, then go through access, environment readiness and the benchmark plan.
00:14 Jared: Yep, sounds good. Jared here.
00:16 Priya: Priya - ML.
00:17 Liam: Liam, ops.
00:19 Carlos: Carlos from Redwood, hey all.
00:21 Maya: Great. So status — last week we asked for VPC peering info and SSO details. Liam, can you give us a quick update on where that is?
00:31 Liam: Yeah, we've got the peering request in, but I need to confirm the exact maintenance window with infra, hoping to get that scheduled tomorrow. Also we have some questions about routing rules, we might need to open a couple of firewall ports, probably 443 and 10250.
00:47 Maya: OK noted. The only thing from our side is we'll need an IP range for the Redwood test nodes and the customer egress. We'll document exact CIDR in the architecture doc I send.
00:59 Carlos: To add — for the dedicated POC runs we prefer doing a short smoke test first — handshake, KV cache warm, health checks — then run the 1k eval. That reduces flakiness.
01:12 Priya: Sounds reasonable. On the data side, we're prepping a 1k sample — mostly user prompts and expected labels. I'll upload to the sheet by Friday. Two questions: one, will tokens be redacted? And two, are there any PII requirements on your side?
01:28 Maya: Good Q. For the hosted flows, we don't persist any customer payloads beyond session caching unless you opt-in; for Dedicated/Private during the POC, we can configure zero-persist and customer-managed KMS. We'll include the SOC 2 and KMS notes in the packet.
01:44 Jared: We're leaning dedicated, but we need to validate latency. Can you run throughput/latency numbers with our prompts? We care about 95th perc latency under 350ms for short prompts.
01:57 Carlos: Yep, that's the plan. Two axes — latency at low QPS and cost at production QPS. We'll run runs with different batch sizes and a quantized model to show tradeoffs. Expect to see improvements in cost with 4-bit quant while latency might change slightly.
02:16 Priya: Are you recommending quant for prod? Concerned about small regressions in quality.
02:21 Carlos: Right — quant is a tradeoff. For many retrieval-augmented generation tasks, 4-bit quant with per-channel scales maintains quality but we should run your eval prompts to confirm. We'll show logits/delta metrics in the benchmark sheet.
02:36 Liam: On access — SSO is via Okta. We can do SAML. Do you need SP metadata or will you give us an IdP flow?
02:45 Maya: We support SAML and OIDC. Send the IdP metadata, Carlos will share our SP metadata.
02:52 Carlos: I'll drop the SP metadata and a short runbook to configure SAML (see https://rwd.co/poc-docs-acme).
03:00 Jared: Another ask — audit logs for requests. We need request-level logging for compliance.
03:07 Maya: We can enable audit logs on Dedicated and Private; logs are stored in your S3 with optional KMS encryption. We'll include retention and format in the doc.
03:16 Priya: Great. For the benchmark, can you also capture token-level cost? That's critical to our ROI calc.
03:23 Carlos: Yep — token-level cost and per-route cost breakdown, we'll add that column to the bench spreadsheet.
03:31 Maya: Quick note on networking: if peering is delayed, there's a fallback to run benchmarks on our hosted sandbox with IP allowlist, but that won't reflect VPC egress cost.
03:42 Liam: Ok, we'll prioritize peering. I'll try to get the window tomorrow and post times to the shared slack.
03:48 Maya: Awesome. Next, results from last week's micro-bench — we saw cold-start latencies of ~420ms on the smaller node, but warm latency around 180-220ms after KV warm. Carlos, any notes?
04:02 Carlos: Yeah, the cold start was higher due to kernel cache warm and initial attention memory alloc. With continuous batching and KV keepalive we saw stable tail latencies in that 180-220ms range for short prompts. For long-context cases latency scales linearly. Also saw token throughput improvements when enabling contiguous memory allocations.
04:22 Priya: Did you test with our prompt template? The template has a 2k context include.
04:27 Carlos: We tested with a mix; for the 2k context you'll see higher mem and slightly higher latency; that's normal. We can surface a recommended config for the model and node type in the doc.
04:40 Maya: On the plan for this week — Carlos will run two benchmark passes: (A) hosted sandbox smoke run with 1k eval, (B) dedicated node run with batching/quant configs once peering is live. We'll compare latency, 95th pct, and token cost.
04:58 Jared: Timeline ok, but we need results by next Wednesday to review with execs.
05:03 Maya: That is doable — Carlos will aim to have preliminary numbers by 2026-11-30.
05:08 Carlos: Yep, prelims by 11/30, final by 12/03 if peering delays happen.
05:14 Liam: One hiccup — we have strict outbound policy, so we might need to set up NAT and allowlist specific endpoints. I'll give you exact egress IPs.
05:25 Maya: Fine. We'll confirm endpoints in the network runbook.
05:29 Priya: Anything on model variants? We had discussed a smaller open model vs a larger one to trade cost/latency.
05:36 Carlos: We'll include run A on rwd-small-v1 and run B on rwd-large-v2 quantized. Also show fallback policy if large model is not available — route to small with slightly different prompts.
05:50 Jared: Competitors — just so you know, our platform team is also running a Bedrock trial and an Anthropic eval, so we'll compare all three on cost and latency.
05:59 Maya: Completely expected. We'll make sure bench sheet shows columns for other vendors so it's easier for your procurement.
06:06 Priya: Quick question — how do you handle KV cache warm across requests from multiple users? We have multi-tenant patterns.
06:15 Carlos: We have per-tenant KV namespaces, and warm on prefix hits. For multi-tenant workloads we recommend pinning tokenization and batching policies per-route so one noisy tenant doesn't hurt others. We'll share recommended configs.
06:29 Jared: Any regulatory concerns — data residency? We're EU data regs on certain flows.
06:35 Maya: For Dedicated we can pin region and for Private on-prem we satisfy full residency. We'll call out region mapping in the packet.
06:44 Priya: Ok great. On scoring — when you run the benchmarks, can you put the exact prompt/expected output pairs in the sheet so we can reproduce?
06:52 Carlos: Yup — every run will include the prompt, gold label, model output, and scoring metric (BLEU/ROUGE/semantic with embedding sim). Some of the metrics are in-house heuristics but we'll document them.
07:06 Maya: Wrapping up — recap of owners and next steps. Maya: send SOC2 + arch diagram (11/27). Carlos: benchmark runs and SP metadata + runbook (11/30). Liam: confirm peering windows and egress IPs (11/26). Priya: upload eval rows and prompt templates (11/27).
07:26 Jared: Sounds good. We'll check back after preliminary numbers.
07:29 Maya: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up in Slack and send calendar invite for the next sync.
07:34 (call ends)
